raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Fixes #61768. A request aborted in the same step its synchronous KV load fails leaves the scheduler before the failure report is processed, so its never-loaded blocks stay prefix-cache hits. This keeps the departing request's block ids until its in-flight outputs arrive, and evicts them when a late failure report names them.

## Claims

- After a sync KV load failure whose owner was aborted in the same step, the invalid block and every block after it are evicted, under both `kv_load_failure_policy` values and with sync and async scheduling. With async scheduling or PP this relies on deferred freeing, which is on for a top-level `kv_consumer`/`kv_both`; see Tradeoffs and limits for a top-level producer whose connector loads.
- A later identical prompt recomputes instead of decoding from never-loaded KV (GPU: r2 cached 1904 → 0, output matches the full-recompute baseline).
- An abort whose load succeeded keeps its valid cached KV (unchanged behavior).

## Validation

**Tests** (`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py`). The four regression tests fail on main at the eviction assertion; with this change all of them pass:

| Test | Role |
|---|---|
| `test_aborted_sync_load_invalid_suffix_evicted` (policy × delayed connector free × PP 1/2) | regression: evicts from the first invalid block; next request hits only the valid prefix |
| `test_aborted_load_survives_other_queued_step` | regression: a batch without a failure keeps the blocks; the later failing batch evicts them |
| `test_aborted_load_survives_empty_schedule` | regression: an empty schedule between the load step and its output keeps the record |
| `test_aborted_sharer_suffix_evicted_by_earlier_batch_failure` | regression: a finished request computed over a block that failed in an earlier batch |
| `test_aborted_successful_sync_load_preserves_cache` | guard: an abort with a successful load keeps the cache |
| `test_finished_request_retained_until_all_outputs_processed` | lifecycle: under async scheduling a record lives until its last in-flight output |

`assert_scheduler_empty` in `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` and `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/utils.py` now also checks the record is empty, so existing tests guard against leaks.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py   # 25 passed
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" pytest --timeout=300 tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/ tests/v1/core/
```

The second command ran on this branch and on main at the same commit (`81e1c3f1`) without this change, with the GPU hidden: the precompiled kernels available locally are for an older commit, so GPU tests can't run meaningfully here and are left to CI. This branch: 2911 passed, 217 failed, 112 errors. Main: 2889 passed, 239 failed, 112 errors. **No test fails on this branch that passes on main.** The only difference is the 22 new tests, which fail on main. The 329 shared failures and errors are mostly tests that need a device, plus a few that already fail on main; all of them fail identically there:

<details>
<summary>Shared failures and errors by file (identical on main without this change)</summary>

| File | Failed + errored |
|---|---|
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py` | 142 |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py` | 101 |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py` | 23 |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py` | 10 |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_worker.py` | 9 |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_bidirectional_kv_transfer.py` | 9 |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hma.py` | 7 |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py` | 5 |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hf3fs_connector.py` | 4 |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py` | 4 |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py` | 3 |
| `tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py` | 2 |
| `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler_e2e.py` | 2 |
| `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` | 2 |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_config.py` | 2 |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_example_connector.py` | 2 |
| `tests/v1/core/test_reset_prefix_cache_e2e.py` | 1 |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py` | 1 |

</details>

**End-to-end** (RTX 5090, Qwen3-0.6B, greedy; harness: [inference-correctness-lab](https://github.com/ArijitDeb/inference-correctness-lab/tree/orphaned-load-failure-v1/cases/orphaned-load-failure), full table: [RESULTS.md](https://github.com/ArijitDeb/inference-correctness-lab/blob/orphaned-load-failure-v1/cases/orphaned-load-failure/RESULTS.md)). The GPU rows measure this patch applied at `04462732` (commit `e23ecfa8`), whose precompiled kernels were available; this branch is the same patch rebased onto current main. Request r1's 1904-token external load is dropped and r1 is aborted inside the same step through `EngineCore.aborts_queue`; r2 repeats the prompt; the baseline is a full recompute. Three trials per cell, `fail` shown, `recompute` identical:

| Tree | Scheduling | r2 cached | r2 == baseline | P(baseline's next token) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main `04462732` | sync | 1904 | 0/3 | 0.0005-0.005 |
| main | async | 1904 | 0/3 | 0.0005-0.005 |
| #53298 at `a7dd070b` merged onto main | sync / async | 1904 | 0/3 | 0.0005-0.005 |
| **this PR** | sync | **0** | **3/3** | **0.962** |
| **this PR** | async | **0** | **3/3** | **0.962** |
| this PR, load succeeds + abort (control) | sync | 1904 | 3/3 | 0.963 |

Baseline P(next) is 0.962. With this change, the new bookkeeping is empty after every trial.

## Details

**Root cause.** `EngineCore.step` and `step_with_batch_queue` apply queued aborts before `update_from_output`. `allocate_slots` hashes blocks at schedule time, before an external load completes, and `free_blocks` keeps hashes. `_handle_invalid_blocks` only looks for affected requests in `running` and `kv_holding_waiting`, so when the owner was freed in between, it returns before evicting.

**Why the request's lifetime isn't enough.** The request object is gone once it is freed, but outputs of the steps that scheduled it can still arrive, and only they carry the failure report. So the departing request's block ids are kept for as long as it has scheduled-but-unprocessed tokens.

**Change** (`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`, +51 lines):
- *Capture:* `_free_request` records the block ids and `num_in_flight_tokens` of a request freed while it still has in-flight tokens, before the delayed-free branch, so connector-delayed and `defer_block_free` paths are covered. Only with a KV connector and a single KV cache group, matching `_handle_invalid_blocks`.
- *Evict:* `_handle_invalid_blocks`, before its early return and under both policies, evicts from the first invalid block onward for every recorded request. The `recompute` no-evict path stays for live owners only: a finished request never recomputes. Every record is checked, not only those in this batch, because a finished request may have computed its own later blocks over a block that failed in an earlier batch.
- *Retire:* `update_from_output` counts each record down by the step's scheduled tokens before its main loop and drops it at zero. It runs before the loop because the loop decrements `num_in_flight_tokens` first, so records created there already exclude this step.

**Relation to other work.** [#42461](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42461) ([RFC #35780](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/35780)) proposes replacing block-level failure reporting with request-level reporting. If it lands, this path and this bug go away with it; until then, every connector that reports `invalid_block_ids` reaches this code, under the default `fail` policy too. PR [#53298](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53298) covers the recompute-policy repair of requests that are still alive; this change covers the owner that is already gone. Against its head `1eca68f4`, `scheduler.py` merges cleanly; both add a line to the test helper `assert_scheduler_empty`, a one-line conflict for whichever lands second.

**Tradeoffs and limits.**
- No GPU work and no host sync: Python bookkeeping only. With sync scheduling, records are created only for requests aborted mid-step. With async scheduling, also for requests that finish while their next batch is in flight; each such record holds a tuple of block ids for one step. A record lives at most `max_concurrent_batches` steps, so the number of records is bounded by the requests that finish within that window. The retire step returns immediately when there are no records; the scan over recorded block ids runs only when a failure is reported.
- Keeping physical block ids, without hashes, requires that a recorded id not identify a different allocation when the failure report is handled. With one batch in flight, nothing allocates between the abort and `update_from_output`, which handles the report and retires the record. With several batches in flight, this holds when `defer_block_free` is on (top-level `kv_consumer`/`kv_both`): the freed blocks are held until the step fence at free time has been processed. Deferred frees may drain before `_handle_invalid_blocks()`, but no scheduling allocation occurs between that drain, failure handling, and record retirement in the normal engine output path. With overlapping batches and a top-level producer whose connector loads, `defer_block_free` is off and a recorded id can be reallocated before the report. In CPU probes this PR then additionally evicts the new allocation's cache entries; the late report failing or rewinding that unrelated request already happens on main (#61905). Whether producer-role loading needs handling before this merges is a call for review.
- Known limit: preempted owners are not tracked here. A consumer-role `reset_prefix_cache(reset_running_requests=True)` can preempt an owner whose load is in flight and then fail to clear the cache, leaving failed-load blocks as prefix hits; producer-role synchronous loaders can also reach this through KV-pressure preemption. Tracked in #61912.
- Multiple KV cache groups are out of scope: `_handle_invalid_blocks` already raises for them, because block ids are only unique within a group.
- Requests still running that share an invalid block are handled by the existing `running` scan; recompute-policy repair ordering for live sharers is #53298's scope.
- The model's next-token distribution is used in validation because greedy equality alone can miss partial corruption.

---

Independent check of this PR with a scheduler fuzzer I've been using on the KV connector paths. It runs on CPU and drives the real `Scheduler` and `KVCacheManager` with a fake connector:
- random sync/async loads that fail some blocks;
- preemption under a small KV pool;
- spec tokens, priority policy and `reset_prefix_cache`;
- a shadow of what each KV slot holds, which flags any read of a slot whose content doesn't match the request's token.

For this PR I added aborts of scheduled requests between `schedule()` and `update_from_output()`, the window in which `_process_aborts_queue` runs.

60 seeds × 300 steps per cell; numbers are seeds with a content mismatch:

| tree | fail + mid-step aborts | fail, no mid-step aborts | recompute + mid-step aborts | recompute, no mid-step aborts |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| parent `81e1c3f183` | 23 | 0 | 13 | 5 |
| this PR `7238ccdf6d` | **0** | 0 | 3 | 5 |
| this PR + #53298 (`1eca68f4a2`, merged locally) | 0 | 0 | **0** | **0** |

- Under the default `fail` policy, the mid-step abort case goes from 23/60 seeds to 0/60.
- Without mid-step aborts, the parent and this PR produce identical action counts, so I see no behavior change outside this case.
- The remaining recompute-policy mismatches are the ones #53298 addresses. With both PRs merged, everything is clean, including 37 (`recompute`) and 83 (`fail`) cases of a sync load failing and the request being aborted in the same step. That matches your description of the two as complementary.
- The merge conflicted only in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/utils.py` (both PRs add asserts to `assert_scheduler_empty`); keeping both resolves it.

Limits: full-attention layout with one KV cache group only, sync scheduling only, CPU only.

(AI-assisted; I ran the fuzzer and checked the results myself.)

Thanks, this is a really useful independent check, and a different method from the GPU repro. The `fail` 23 → 0 with no change in action counts without mid-step aborts is exactly what the change should do. On the 3 remaining `recompute` seeds: I'd expect those to be aborts that land after the failure report was processed (owner truncated, then gone before recomputing), which is #53298's case rather than this one; your 0 with both merged fits that.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

🚀

Independent check of this PR with a scheduler fuzzer I've been using on the KV connector paths. It runs on CPU and drives the real `Scheduler` and `KVCacheManager` with a fake connector:
- random sync/async loads that fail some blocks;
- preemption under a small KV pool;
- spec tokens, priority policy and `reset_prefix_cache`;
- a shadow of what each KV slot holds, which flags any read of a slot whose content doesn't match the request's token.

For this PR I added aborts of scheduled requests between `schedule()` and `update_from_output()`, the window in which `_process_aborts_queue` runs.

60 seeds × 300 steps per cell; numbers are seeds with a content mismatch:

| tree | fail + mid-step aborts | fail, no mid-step aborts | recompute + mid-step aborts | recompute, no mid-step aborts |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| parent `81e1c3f183` | 23 | 0 | 13 | 5 |
| this PR `7238ccdf6d` | **0** | 0 | 3 | 5 |
| this PR + #53298 (`1eca68f4a2`, merged locally) | 0 | 0 | **0** | **0** |

- Under the default `fail` policy, the mid-step abort case goes from 23/60 seeds to 0/60.
- Without mid-step aborts, the parent and this PR produce identical action counts, so I see no behavior change outside this case.
- The remaining recompute-policy mismatches are the ones #53298 addresses. With both PRs merged, everything is clean, including 37 (`recompute`) and 83 (`fail`) cases of a sync load failing and the request being aborted in the same step. That matches your description of the two as complementary.
- The merge conflicted only in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/utils.py` (both PRs add asserts to `assert_scheduler_empty`); keeping both resolves it.

Limits: full-attention layout with one KV cache group only, sync scheduling only, CPU only.

(AI-assisted; I ran the fuzzer and checked the results myself.)

Thanks, this is a really useful independent check, and a different method from the GPU repro. The `fail` 23 → 0 with no change in action counts without mid-step aborts is exactly what the change should do. On the 3 remaining `recompute` seeds: I'd expect those to be aborts that land after the failure report was processed (owner truncated, then gone before recomputing), which is #53298's case rather than this one; your 0 with both merged fits that.
